# Publishing a post

Keep writing in Google Docs if that is comfortable. This site has a visual editor so you do not need to edit Markdown, YAML, HTML, or GitHub files by hand.

1. Open [Pages CMS](https://app.pagescms.org/), sign in with GitHub, and select **BenCBanks/bencbanks.github.io** on the **master** branch.
2. Open **Blog posts** and choose **New**. Add a title, a one or two sentence summary, and your post. You can paste text from Google Docs into the rich-text editor. Check headings, links, and lists after pasting.
3. Add a topic and, if you want one, a project image. If you add an image, fill in **Image description**. Posts without images display as clean text-only rows.
4. Save with **Publish on the website** turned **off**. This stores a draft in GitHub without showing it on the public site.
5. When ready, reread the post, turn **Publish on the website** **on**, and save. GitHub Pages rebuilds the site automatically. Open the Projects page afterward to check the result.

To correct a published post, edit it in Pages CMS and save. Turning the publish switch off hides the post without deleting its file. Renaming and deleting posts are disabled in the editor to prevent accidental broken links.

The two older essays contain custom HTML. Use the editor's **Source** mode for changes to their complex sections, or ask for help until we verify how the visual editor preserves that HTML.

## Choosing what to write

Pick one question a visitor might have about your work or a project. Write down a concrete example and what you learned. A short note can be 300–600 words; a project story can be 700–1,200. Use more space when a chart or technical decision needs it. These are writing guides, not search-engine rules.

Simple outline: **The question → What I tried → What happened → What I would do differently.**
